project.name: Derma_AI Evidence Atlas
project.subtitle: Explainable Dermatology AI · CBM + clinician-in-the-loop RL + fairness monitoring
project.tagline: From a promising prototype to defensible research evidence.
project.north_star: Test whether concept-based explanations, fairness-aware triage, and reviewed clinician feedback improve reliability and equity over a standard transfer-learning baseline, without pretending the system is clinically validated.
project.disclaimer: Research and educational use only. Not a medical device, not a clinical diagnosis system, and not a basis for treatment decisions. Qualified clinicians must review any real-world use.

snapshot.scope: Remote repository contents and GitHub check metadata inspected. Local 15/15 PASSION and 11/11 definition-of-done results are reported, not independently reproduced in this audit.

status_legend.done: Acceptance criteria met with inspectable evidence
status_legend.partial: Implementation exists, but validation or integration is incomplete
status_legend.reported: A result was reported, but not independently reproduced here
status_legend.blocked: Requires an external resource, permission, person, or decision
status_legend.failed: A verified contradiction or broken acceptance contract

gates.name: Reproducibility gate
gates.rule: A clean clone must run the declared tests and readiness checks without copied files; the exact pushed commit must have a green CI run.

gates.name: Data rights & ethics gate
gates.rule: Licences, access terms, de-identification, retention, and IRB/REC determination must be documented before restricted or local patient data are used.

gates.name: Real KS cohort gate
gates.rule: Kaposi sarcoma training requires real, permissioned, clinician-reviewed images. Synthetic images may support smoke tests, not a real-data claim.

gates.name: Concept supervision gate
gates.rule: The seven concepts need agreed definitions, observable labels or an explicit weak-supervision design, and clinician review before concept scores are presented as meaningful.

gates.name: Evaluation integrity gate
gates.rule: Lock leakage-free splits, evaluate diagnosis and triage separately, report uncertainty and missing strata, and never tune on the test set.

gates.name: Human-use safety gate
gates.rule: No silent mock diagnosis, honest readiness, reviewed offline updates, rollback, privacy controls, and explicit ethics/stakeholder approval before any real-world pilot.

explanation.title: 1. What this project is
paragraphs: Derma_AI is a research prototype for explainable, equity-aware dermatology triage in Uganda/East Africa. It combines a concept-bottleneck image classifier, a small reinforcement-learning triage policy, clinician feedback, fairness monitoring, and a web dashboard.

The research question is comparative: do concept supervision, fairness-weighted triage, and reviewed offline feedback improve reliability and equity over a standard transfer-learning baseline under constrained labels and bandwidth? The project is not currently a validated diagnostic product.
bullets: Target conditions in code: benign, melanoma, and Kaposi sarcoma.
Target triage actions in code: routine, follow-up, and urgent.
Planned clinical context: Uganda Cancer Institute and Mbarara Hospital, subject to real agreements and approvals.
Current boundary: research/education only; no autonomous diagnosis or treatment decision.

explanation.title: 2. End-to-end pipeline
paragraphs: An image and metadata enter a deterministic preprocessing path. HRNet-W18 extracts visual features; a seven-output bottleneck is intended to represent clinical concepts; a linear head maps those concepts to three diagnosis classes. A separate PPO-style policy receives seven concept scores plus a six-value Fitzpatrick encoding and chooses one of three triage actions.

A clinician can review the output and submit a correction. Corrections enter an offline buffer; a candidate policy update must be evaluated and approved before promotion. The dashboard and fairness tracker record outcomes, overrides, subgroup counts, and audit information. Heatmaps are supporting model evidence, not clinical proof.
bullets: Input → quality/permission checks → preprocessing → HRNet features.
Features → seven concept scores → three class logits.
Concepts + skin-tone encoding → triage policy → proposed lane.
Clinician review → correction buffer → offline candidate update → validation → promote or rollback.
Cases and predictions → fairness/uncertainty reports → research dashboard and export.

explanation.title: 4. Data strategy that matches the labels
paragraphs: The datasets cannot be blended as though they describe the same task. HAM10000 is dermoscopic and has no real Kaposi sarcoma class. PASSION contains inflammatory/infectious conditions and is used here as an external fairness/escalation cohort, not as benign/melanoma/KS ground truth. Fitzpatrick17k is a possible source of real KS-labelled candidates, but access and clinician audit are required. SKINCON can supply some expert concept annotations, not a complete match for the seven project concepts.

explanation.title: 5. What counts as evidence
paragraphs: Use a locked, group-aware train/validation/test design. Select models on validation data, then evaluate frozen candidates on sealed test data. Compare a standard classifier, a concept-supervised CBM, fairness-weighted triage, and reviewed feedback under matched conditions. Report uncertainty and subgroup counts; preserve negative results.
bullets: Diagnosis: per-class sensitivity/specificity, balanced accuracy, discrimination where valid, calibration, confidence intervals.
Triage: critical-miss rate, over-triage, lane agreement, and clinician-reviewed outcomes.
Fairness: subgroup TPR/FNR gaps with counts and uncertainty; pre-specified trade-offs rather than post-hoc thresholds.
Concepts: expert agreement, intervention effect, and attribution sanity checks.
Human loop: override reasons, review time, update rejection/rollback, and simulated versus real feedback distinction.
PASSION: predicted escalation distributions by subject/condition/skin tone only; not diagnostic accuracy.

explanation.title: 6. Decisions that protect the research
paragraphs: These are design risks, not reasons to abandon the project. They determine whether the final claims are credible.
bullets: Domain shift: dermoscopic HAM images and clinical atlas/phone photographs are not interchangeable.
Concept observability: diameter needs scale; pigment intensity is not a validated Fitzpatrick diagnosis.
Single-step RL: the current environment is closer to a contextual bandit; PPO must earn its complexity through comparison.
Override-only feedback is selected data; clinician action is not automatically pathology ground truth.
Skin-tone multipliers encode a value judgment and require clinician review plus over-triage analysis.
Fallback diagnosis is a safety hazard even if renamed from mock to fallback.
Small KS samples may support a feasibility study, not a broad clinical performance claim.
IRB exemption, data licence, and stakeholder interest are three different permissions.

explanation.title: 7. Four different meanings of done
paragraphs: Use separate finish lines so a UI milestone cannot masquerade as training or clinical readiness.

rows: Declared contracts work in a clean clone and exact-head CI
Reproducible real-data candidate, hash, config, and validation report
Sealed-test comparisons, fairness, ablations, limitations, and review
Separate ethics/regulatory approval, safety case, monitoring, and stop rules

explanation.title: 8. How to keep the roadmap alive
paragraphs: Use the dashboard for exploration and the JSON file for versioned truth. A task is done only when its acceptance criteria have evidence. Browser edits are local drafts until exported, reviewed, and committed.
bullets: Daily: update the one task you moved; add a commit, run ID, report path, or decision reference.
Weekly: review blockers, choose the next three moves, and rebuild the dashboard/Markdown from JSON.
At a gate: attach the evidence, name the reviewer, and record the decision; do not convert blocked to done by optimism.
When a result changes scope: add a changelog entry and update dependent tasks rather than silently rewriting history.
Never store patient data, secrets, raw restricted images, or access tokens in the tracker.
